title: Working Music Theory: Practical Harmony and Song Analysis
summary: A 4-week, step-by-step practical music theory course designed for solo learners. Focuses on building scales, decoding intervals and chords, analyzing song progressions with Roman numerals, and transposing music for real-world performance and composition.

weeks.theme: Pitches, Rhythm, and the Major Scale Architecture

days.title: The 12 Pitches, Semitones, and Whole Steps
objectives: Identify the 12 chromatic pitches and their enharmonic equivalents on a keyboard layout
Calculate intervals of whole steps and half steps between specified note pairs

days.title: Rhythm Values, Meters, and Time Signatures
objectives: Calculate beat values for combinations of whole, half, quarter, eighth, and sixteenth notes
Identify measure groupings in standard 4/4, 3/4, and 6/8 time signatures

days.title: The Major Scale Formula
objectives: Spell any major scale using the whole-step and half-step pattern (W-W-H-W-W-W-H)
Write out scale degree numbers and note names for C, G, D, and F major

days.title: Key Signatures and the Circle of Fifths
objectives: Determine the number of sharps or flats in any key signature using the Circle of Fifths
Identify the root key from standard treble and bass clef key signatures

days.title: Intervals Part 1: Seconds, Thirds, and Octaves
objectives: Calculate interval size and quality for major, minor, and perfect seconds and thirds
Spell the correct note a major or minor third above a given root note

weeks.theme: Intervals, Minor Keys, and Triad Construction

days.title: Intervals Part 2: Fourths, Fifths, Sixths, and Sevenths
objectives: Classify perfect fourths, perfect fifths, tritones, and major/minor sixths and sevenths
Invert any simple interval and name the resulting interval size and quality

days.title: The Natural Minor Scale and Relative Keys
objectives: Derive the natural minor scale using its relative major counterpart
Spell natural minor scales using the interval formula (W-H-W-W-H-W-W)

days.title: Harmonic and Melodic Minor Scales
objectives: Construct harmonic and melodic minor scales for any given root
Explain why the 7th degree is raised in minor key compositions to create a leading tone

days.title: Building Major and Minor Triads
objectives: Construct major and minor triads using root, third, and fifth intervals
Spell triad chords from standard lead sheet chord symbols (e.g., C, Am, F#m, Eb)

days.title: Diminished Triads, Augmented Triads, and Inversions
objectives: Build diminished and augmented triads using stacked intervals
Identify root position, first inversion, and second inversion slash chords

weeks.theme: Diatonic Harmony, Roman Numerals, and Seventh Chords

days.title: Diatonic Triads in Major Keys
objectives: Assign Roman numerals (I through vii°) to all seven diatonic triads in any major key
Identify whether each scale degree triad in a major key is major, minor, or diminished

days.title: Standard Chord Progressions and Cadences
objectives: Analyze popular chord progressions using Roman numerals (e.g., I-V-vi-IV and ii-V-I)
Identify authentic, plagal, half, and deceptive cadences in short musical excerpts

days.title: Diatonic Triads in Minor Keys
objectives: Construct diatonic triads for natural and harmonic minor scales using Roman numerals
Explain why the minor key V chord is commonly altered to a major triad

days.title: Seventh Chords: Major 7, Dominant 7, and Minor 7
objectives: Construct Major 7th, Dominant 7th, Minor 7th, and Half-Diminished 7th chords
Translate seventh chord lead sheet symbols (e.g., Cmaj7, G7, Am7, Bm7b5) into note spellings

days.title: Voice Leading Principles and Reading Lead Sheets
objectives: Arrange triad transitions using voice leading rules that minimize note movement
Read and interpret a single-page lead sheet containing melody and chord symbols

days.title: Transposition Techniques
objectives: Transpose a chord progression to a new key using Roman numeral analysis
Transpose a melodic line to accommodate a different vocal or instrumental range

days.title: Secondary Dominants
objectives: Identify secondary dominant chords (such as V/V and V/vi) within chord charts
Write a secondary dominant chord that targets a specified diatonic destination chord

days.title: Borrowed Chords and Modal Interchange
objectives: Identify chords borrowed from the parallel minor in major-key songs (e.g., minor iv, bVI)
Explain the emotional contrast produced by borrowed chords in modern songwriting

days.title: Everyday Modes: Dorian, Mixolydian, and Aeolian
objectives: Differentiate Dorian and Mixolydian modes from standard major and natural minor scales
Identify characteristic modal scale degrees and modal chord vamp patterns

days.title: Full Song Harmonic Analysis
objectives: Perform an end-to-end Roman numeral analysis on a complete pop or film song chart
Identify tonic key centers, borrowed chords, voice leading shifts, and cadence points
